requirements.source_text: 1. Every permit/application has its own checklist
2. Checklist is sent to the client
3. Documents are validated individually
4. Valid documents go to the server immediately
5. Missing documents are tracked independently
6. Incorrect documents are not silently accepted
7. The server is the operational source of truth for collected documents
8. Document collection and engineering must operate in parallel
9. Technical report is part of the submission package
10. Engineering supplies the substantive project description
11. Technical report contains fixed identity fields
12. Municipality source determines municipality
13. Plot number comes from authoritative property documentation
14. Municipality comments create a revision loop
15. Comments may require engineering + document/report revision
16. Municipality comment is not necessarily a full rejection
17. The system must preserve revision history
18. Permit types matter
19. Industrial Area applications have special documents
20. Industrial croqui has a specific authority meaning
21. Previous permits/completion/plans can be prerequisites
22. Ownership can involve many parties
23. Company ownership requires company evidence
24. Authorized representative / power of attorney matters
25. Deceased owner ≠ request deceased owner's ID
26. Number of heirs can be large
27. Expired IDs must be detected and followed up
28. Partial correction is required
29. Signature/stamp requirements depend on legal party type
30. Municipality portal upload is deliberately NOT a current requirement
Every eligible project/contract has a governed Billing Plan.
The Billing Plan comes from exact Contract/payment-condition truth.
Every installment has sequence, amount/percentage and trigger.
Supervision supports a fixed recurring monthly billing plan.
Design supports event/milestone-driven billing.
Each installment can have a planned collection/forecast date.
Forecast collection date is distinct from invoice due date.
Actual collection date is separately recorded.
Management can compare planned vs actual collection.
Project financial balance/collected/remaining values are system-derived—not manually maintained.
Engineering/Project Manager initiates a Billing Request when the milestone is achieved.
Billing/Admin does not blindly trust the request.
Billing/Admin checks the project's quotation/contract payment conditions.
Billing/Admin verifies that the requested milestone exists.
Billing/Admin verifies the amount/percentage.
Billing/Admin verifies correct milestone sequence.
Trigger evidence is attached/pinned.
A later milestone cannot silently jump an earlier required project milestone.
Explicit exceptions must be governed rather than silently bypassing sequence.
New project → use governed standard invoice template.
Existing project → “Create Next Invoice” from the same project's previous invoice/context.
Do not copy an unrelated project's invoice and retype project information.
Allocate the next global AMEC invoice reference.
Maintain a separate per-project installment number: 01, 02, 03...

Produce the design evidence pack.

Include the authority/system proof supporting the milestone.
Supervision invoice can remain simpler than design invoice.
Preserve exact issued invoice immutability.
Maintain governed Word/DOCX and PDF outputs if AMEC intends to retain today's dual-file operational requirement.
Draft acceptance and actual issue are separate human actions.
Issued invoice receives the official company number.
Invoice delivery is a separate event from issuance.
Delivery evidence policy depends on channel.
Email delivery retains sent-email proof.
WhatsApp requires retained acknowledgment/response evidence.
Messenger delivery requires returned signed/received-invoice proof.
Missing external proof generates an unresolved follow-up/task.
Invoice cannot be considered evidence-complete while mandatory delivery proof is missing.
Receipt/payment is recorded against exact Contract/Project/Invoice context.
Record actual received date.
Record amount.
Record currency.
Record payment method.
Record payment reference.
Record where/who actually received the money.
Support corporate-bank transfer.
Support cheque.
Support exceptional approved receipt through another custodian/account, such as the Engineer Mohammed example.
Payment evidence is mandatory before verification.
Transfer requires transfer evidence.
Cheque requires the cheque image and AMEC receipt/voucher.
Personal/alternate-recipient collection requires suitable receipt/transfer confirmation.
Payment observation ≠ payment verification.
Payment verification ≠ allocation.
Partial payment remains partial and leaves outstanding balance.
Over-allocation must be blocked.
Wrong payment/collection must have a governed reversal/correction path.
Reversal must undo dependent receivable effects without deleting audit history.
An issued invoice may remain unpaid.
An unpaid invoice can be disputed/problematic.
AMEC may deliberately waive/release/write off a receivable.
Waiver/write-off must be a separate protected human action.
It must not masquerade as PAID.
Original invoice remains in history.
Original outstanding amount remains historically visible.
Resolution reason/evidence/authority must be recorded.
Downstream balance/reporting must understand the waived amount.
Outstanding invoice can have collection follow-ups.
Missing delivery proof can have separate follow-ups.
External dependencies such as Hisham must remain visible until fulfilled.
Every invoice needs an evidence-completeness state.
Every invoice needs a receivable-resolution state.

All financially required project installments resolved → Billing Complete / Financially Collected.
Billing Complete does not automatically mean Engineering/Project Completion.
Project lifecycle completion remains its own protected human process.
The Project workspace should visibly display its financial/billing completion condition.
Billing operator does not manually touch accounting/formula internals.
Verified collection/resolution should feed downstream financial reporting deterministically.
Wrong/reversed collection must reverse those downstream effects.
Revenue, expense, profit and receivable reporting must therefore consume governed financial events.
ProposalOps Billing itself should not silently pretend to be the accounting journal if accounting remains a separate domain/system.
